title: Gigerenzer's Depth Psychology & The Soul's History

concepts.title: Immanent vs. External Reflection: The Methodological Foundation of Psychology
concepts.excerpt: There is a fundamental methodological divide in how consciousness can approach any phenomenon.

concepts.title: Two Senses of Meaning: The Ontological vs. Utilitarian Divide
concepts.excerpt: Contemporary consciousness has collapsed meaning into a single sense—the utilitarian.

concepts.title: Soul Events as Events of Meaning: Consciousness, Psychology, and the Intrinsic Logic of Phenomena
concepts.excerpt: Psychology as a discipline rests on a presupposition so fundamental that it is almost never stated: Soul phenomena have the intrinsic property of consciousness.

concepts.title: The Sacrifice of Isaac as Watershed: Where Consciousness Irreversibly Divides
concepts.excerpt: On one side of the watershed: The archaic world where sacrifice is soul-making, where the killing of the first-born son is apotheosis, where the sacred act reaches its apex in ritual slaughter.

concepts.title: Psychology's Emergence: The Inversion That Created Modern Consciousness
concepts.excerpt: There is a precise historical moment when something unprecedented happens in human consciousness.

concepts.title: The Child as Logical Form: The Consciousness Configuration That Enables Soul-Work
concepts.excerpt: When Gigerenzer speaks of "the child," he does not mean literal children.

concepts.title: Methodological Violence: How Consciousness Kills the Child and Calls It Development
concepts.excerpt: Gigerenzer names a paradox so fundamental it reorders everything we think we know about human development: genuine soul-making requires killing—requires violence, rupture, the destruction of existing structures.

concepts.title: Wolfgang Gigerenzer: Biographical and Intellectual Background
concepts.excerpt: Wolfgang Gigerenzer is a practicing Jungian analyst trained in the Swiss Jungian tradition, bringing 30+ years of clinical experience alongside rigorous philosophical study.

concepts.title: Burkert's Homo Necans: Killing as Foundational to Humanity
concepts.excerpt: Walter Burkert's thesis in Homo Necans (1972) is deceptively simple: killing is not incidental to human nature.

concepts.title: Girard's Scapegoat Mechanism: Sacrifice and the Foundation of Social Order
concepts.excerpt: René Girard's thesis (developed across Violence and the Sacred and subsequent works): human culture originates in a single mechanism—collective killing.

concepts.title: Firstborn Sacrifice: Archetypal Practice and Consciousness Transformation
concepts.excerpt: The practice of sacrificing the firstborn—especially the firstborn child—is documented across numerous ancient civilizations:

concepts.title: Islamic Terrorism: Repressed Sacrificial Consciousness Manifest
concepts.excerpt: Contemporary analysis treats Islamic terrorism primarily through political, economic, or ideological frames.

concepts.title: The Three Stances: How Consciousness Encounters Its Other and Generates Reality
concepts.excerpt: At the core of Gigerenzer's psychological vision is a single, devastating question: What happens when consciousness encounters something that negates it?

concepts.title: Fairytale and Archetypal Methodology: How Consciousness Generates Reality Through Stance
concepts.excerpt: Gigerenzer's most sophisticated methodological contribution is his reading of fairytales as expressions of logical and psychological structures that reveal how consciousness generates reality rather than merely perceiving it.

concepts.title: Shadow as First Psychological Inwardization: The Apprentice-Piece
concepts.excerpt: The shadow is consciousness's first psychological encounter with genuine otherness within itself.

concepts.title: Anima-Animus and the Masterpiece of Psychology
concepts.excerpt: Gigerenzer uses medieval craft terminology to describe psychological development.

concepts.title: Animus as Pure Negation: The Force That Will Not Obey
concepts.excerpt: The animus is not a thing. It is not a quality consciousness can develop or integrate.

concepts.title: Soul Versus Psyche: The Distinction That Defines Psychology's Mission
concepts.excerpt: Contemporary psychology uses "psyche" and "soul" as synonyms. Gigerenzer insists they are fundamentally different, and this distinction is the key to understanding what psychology actually is and what it fails to do.

concepts.title: Killing Versus Murder: The Psychology of Deliberate Harm
concepts.excerpt: Contemporary psychology conflates killing and murder, treating all violence as pathological.

concepts.title: Sacrifice as Soul-Making: Primordial and Necessary
concepts.excerpt: Sacrifice is not driven by practical utility. Ritual sacrificeâ€”the deliberate killing of animals or humans in religious contextsâ€”appears across all civilizations independent of economic need.

concepts.title: First-Order vs. Second-Order Killings: The Soul's Historical Differentiation
concepts.excerpt: When we watch human history, we notice something strange: We don't encounter a single kind of killing.

concepts.title: Christianity: Preservation of the Child—Civilizational Inversion
concepts.excerpt: Every civilization before Christianity organized itself around a principle: initiation requires killing the child.

concepts.title: Separation of Heaven and Earth: Sacrifice as Cosmological Act
concepts.excerpt: In every creation myth, something must die for form to emerge. Not metaphorically—but as the primal act that separates undifferentiated being from specific manifestation.

concepts.title: Necessity of Regularly Repeated Sacrifice: Entropy and Soul-Maintenance
concepts.excerpt: Anthropologists have long puzzled over a feature of archaic civilization that modernity finds almost incomprehensible: sacrifice was not an occasional event.

concepts.title: Emancipation From Sacrifice: Second-Order Killings and Modernity's Self-Definition
concepts.excerpt: Something extraordinary happens in the centuries leading to modernity: a civilization becomes conscious of its own sacrificial foundation and decides to reject it.

concepts.title: Money as Modern God: Virtual Reality and Incarnationless Faith
concepts.excerpt: Christianity, as Gigerenzer reads it, made an unprecedented theological move: it posited a God who is not incarnate.

concepts.title: Psychology's Platonism Problem: Privileging Forms Over Manifestation
concepts.excerpt: Contemporary psychology, especially depth psychology, has inherited a structural disease from Western metaphysics: Platonism.

concepts.title: Direct Engagement With Soul vs. Therapeutic Evasion: The Incompatible Enterprises
concepts.excerpt: Here is the deepest problem: genuine psychology and therapy are not the same thing.

concepts.title: Hillman vs. Gigerenzer: Imaginal Psychology and Concrete Manifestation
concepts.excerpt: James Hillman and Wolfgang Gigerenzer both claim to honor the soul. Both insist that contemporary psychology has become too clinical, too reductive, too hostile to the depths.

concepts.title: Consciousness and Reality: How Stance Constitutes World
concepts.excerpt: Gigerenzer makes a claim that sounds absurd to modern consciousness: reality is not independent of the stance consciousness takes toward it.

concepts.title: Christ as Final Sacrifice: Unresolved Paradox and Christianity's Shadow
concepts.excerpt: Christianity claims to abolish sacrifice. This is its revolutionary move: God no longer demands sacrifice.

concepts.title: Jung and Japanese Philosophy: Type, Emptiness, and the Way
concepts.excerpt: Jung was fascinated by Zen Buddhism, particularly its insistence that truth cannot be grasped through rational thinking.

concepts.title: Jung and Taoism: The Psychology of Wu Wei and Complementary Opposites
concepts.excerpt: In Taoism, the Tao is the fundamental reality—the source of all manifestation, utterly beyond description or naming.

concepts.title: Jung and Vedic Psychology: Parallel Structures of Self and Consciousness
concepts.excerpt: Jung was reading the Upanishads when he developed his psychological model.

concepts.title: Authentic Motivation as Unifying Principle — Across Psychology, Spirituality, Creativity, and Institutions
concepts.excerpt: Psychology alone explains the mechanism: intrinsic motivation generates sustained engagement, flow states, and better outcomes than extrinsic motivation.

concepts.title: Darwin's Life as Case Study: The Man Who Couldn't See His Own Mind
concepts.excerpt: Charles Darwin spent his life studying human nature without becoming substantially more self-aware about his own motivations.

concepts.title: Free Will & Moral Responsibility: Agency in a Determined System
concepts.excerpt: Evolutionary psychology describes humans as products of selection—shaped by millions of years of pressure to survive and reproduce.

concepts.title: Loving Combat / Agonistic Engagement: Fierce Opposition Without Dehumanization
concepts.excerpt: Common thinking presents a false binary: either you have conflict (which requires enmity, dehumanization, domination) or you have peace (which requires capitulation, the absence of real disagreement).

concepts.title: Mēsis as Internal Sabotage: The Cunning Against the Self
concepts.excerpt: The ancient Greek distinction between mēsis (cunning intelligence) and biē (brute force) names a fundamental strategic choice: overcoming opposition through intelligence, deception, and positioning rather than through direct power.

concepts.title: Serene Judgment Under Uncertainty: The Epistemology of Decisive Action
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a commander in darkness hearing distant sounds — hoofbeats, shouts, the percussion of conflict.
